prompt.brief: Design a geo-discovery service that finds nearby places or opted-in friends, supports category/filter/ranking queries, and remains accurate and low-latency as locations and updates change.
successSignals: Define place and friend location freshness, consent/visibility, radius semantics, filters, ranking, pagination, and geospatial index updates.
Use cells/geohashes or equivalent partitioning, expand search rings for sparse areas, and control hot urban cells and popular queries.
Separate location writes and place ingestion from query serving; explain stale positions, privacy deletion, and cache invalidation.
Cover abuse, spoofed locations, regional failure, observability, and a safe empty/stale-result mode.

functional: Update opted-in friend locations and place metadata, then query nearby results by radius, category, rating, availability, and distance.
Support privacy controls, blocked users, location TTLs, pagination, ranking explanations, map clusters, and place edits.
Make updates retry-safe, remove expired/deleted locations, rebuild indexes, and degrade to coarse or cached results during outages.
nonFunctional: Meet p95 nearby-query latency under 150ms and never expose a friend location beyond its consent freshness window.
Scale to 100M places/users and dense-city query hotspots without a single hot key or unbounded synchronous work.
Do not lose committed state; make retries and duplicate events safe.
Degrade safely when downstream workers, caches, or external dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: 100M places/users and 1M location updates per second at peak
Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Geo-discovery service commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Geo-discovery service writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Geo-discovery service version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Geo-discovery service by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Geo-discovery service work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Geo-discovery service projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Geo-discovery service projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Geo-discovery service records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Geo-discovery service latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
